_comment: SSRF guard for outbound HTTP (ADR-0084). Feature F7.
The Api client and Web Push refuse, by default, to connect to a private or
internal address. Before each connection - the initial URL AND every redirect
hop the Api client follows - the host is resolved to its IP address(es) and the
request is refused if ANY resolved address is loopback, private, link-local
(including the cloud metadata address 169.254.169.254), unspecified or CGNAT.
A non-http(s) scheme is refused. The operator opt-out is TINA4_ALLOW_PRIVATE_REQUESTS
(truthy = allow), off by default, with the same truthiness in all four frameworks;
an app may also pass an explicit allow-list of hosts / host:port / CIDRs.
The guard does NOT apply to the built-in dev/test servers that bind 0.0.0.0
(that is inbound), only to the outbound Api client and Web Push.
Residual TOCTOU: the guard resolves-then-connects; the language HTTP clients
re-resolve on connect, so a validated public address could in theory be rebound
to a private one in the window between the two lookups. It is narrowed by
blocking when ANY resolved address is private and by re-validating on every
redirect hop; it is not fully closed because none of the four stock HTTP clients
lets Tina4 pin the exact validated IP for the socket while keeping TLS SNI and
the Host header. See ADR-0084.
addresses[]: each is fed to the real classifier. blocked=true means the guard
must refuse it by default. category is documentation only.
truthy_opt_out[]: values that, trimmed and lower-cased, turn TINA4_ALLOW_PRIVATE_REQUESTS on.
Shared suite names: Python tests/test_ssrf_guard_contract.py, PHP
tests/SsrfGuardContractTest.php, Ruby spec/ssrf_guard_contract_spec.rb, Node
test/ssrfGuardContract.test.ts. Each keeps a copy of this file under its own
fixtures dir and drives the real classifier + a real loopback listener - no mocks.
feature: F7 - outbound SSRF guard for the Api client and Web Push

redirect_hops.name: public-listener-302s-to-metadata
redirect_hops.note: the initial loopback listener is reached via an explicit allow-list entry; the 302 target is not on the allow-list and is refused at the hop

invariants.rule: The address classifier refuses loopback, private (10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16, fc00::/7), link-local (169.254/16, fe80::/10) including 169.254.169.254, unspecified (0.0.0.0, ::) and CGNAT (100.64/10), including IPv4-mapped IPv6; it allows public addresses. A non-http(s) scheme is refused.

By default the Api client refuses a request to a private/internal address and refuses a redirect hop to one; with TINA4_ALLOW_PRIVATE_REQUESTS truthy the same requests succeed; the block error names the opt-out env var. Web Push refuses a private endpoint unless opted in.
cases: api blocks request to loopback by default
api allows request with opt out
api blocks redirect hop to private
web push blocked to private endpoint unless opted in
